newsitem.title: GREECE: UPDATE: THOUSANDS OF GREEK FARMERS MARCH THROUGH ATHENS.
newsitem.headline: UPDATE: THOUSANDS OF GREEK FARMERS MARCH THROUGH ATHENS.

text.p: Thousands of Greek farmers marched trough central Athens towards parliament to press demands for cheaper fuel and higher state subsidies for their produce.

Police said more than 6,000 had gathered at Athens' Vathis Square before starting the march. Some were construction workers and students but most were farmers who arrived in scores of buses from the countryside.
The farmers, who have blocked Greek highways for 22 days, want to meet Prime Minister Costas Simitis, who has refused to see them until they abandon their barricades.
Minister to the Prime Minister George Paschalides was expected to meet the farmers instead.
Several thousand police reinforcements have been called up in Athens to control the march and to prevent the farmers from reaching Simitis's central office at Megaro Maximou.
Riot police were heavy in the area around the presidential palace and the Rigilis area where the prime minister's office is located. They have said the protesters will not be allowed through.

The buses, coming in from Larissa and further north, have halted almost all traffic around Omonia Square. Police appealed on radio and television for people to avoid driving in Athens' centre. --Dina Kyriakidou, Athens Newsroom +301 3311812-4
